title: VPD officers cleared of wrongdoing in 2009 shooting death of man
article: Two external investigations have cleared Vancouver police officers of any wrongdoing in a 2009 domestic-dispute call that saw a knife-wielding 46-year-old Vancouver man shot dead in front of his 13-year-old daughter.

At 9:30 p.m. on Friday, Sept. 18, 2009, Eugene Anthony Knight was shot by two officers after a third officer shot him with a Taser that proved "ineffective," Sgt. Peter Thiessen, Integrated Homicide Investigation Team spokesman, told The Province at the time.

Knight's wife, also 46, had called 911, screaming that a knife-wielding man was threatening to kill her, police said. Three officers broke through Knight's door at 102-2572 Birch Street within four minutes of the call. They ordered Knight to drop the knife, Thiessen said, at the time.
Neighbours interviewed at the time told The Province that violent screams and up to six shots shattered the calm of the quiet, tree-lined South Granville block.
Both neighbours and police said it was not the first domestic disturbance in the home.
Vancouver police asked an external police agency to investigate.
After a lengthy investigation, IHIT found the fatal shooting was not a criminal act, Thiessen said in a news release today.

The case was not forwarded to Crown counsel. As a matter of process, the file was forwarded to the Office of the Police Complaint Commission (OPCC) for an independent review. Rollie Woods of the OPCC said his office oversaw a Police Act investigation into the shooting, conducted by Port Moody police.
That investigation also found no wrongdoing.
"There was no criminality or Police Act (issues) in this tragic event," Woods said, in an interview. "Everything (found by IHIT), there was evidence to support it."
A Coroner's inquest has been scheduled.
Thiessen referred all questions to the Coroner's office, which has not immediately returned calls.

At the time, Thiessen said Knight's wife was not physically harmed in the knife-wielding incident and was transported to the Vancouver police detachment, along with her daughter. The wife was co-operating with police and counselling was being provided to both, police said.

The officer who fired a Taser at Knight had 18 years service with the Vancouver police. The two officers who shot Knight had 10 years and nine months experience with the VPD, respectively, police said.
